core/tokens/starfield/params/scene.ts

Scene-shell and fallback parameters — the skybox radius,
Source src/core/tokens/starfield/params/scene.ts
UX surface Shared primitives every surface builds on — no direct UI.

Members

STAR_DENSITY

One star per N² css px of surface area.

STAR_MAX

Hard cap so 8K displays don't allocate thousands of arcs.

STAR_SIZE_MAX

Brightest star radius in css px (most stars draw smaller).

GLINT_RATIO

Fraction of stars that get a diffraction-cross glint.

BAND_STARS

Extra micro-stars densified along the milky band.

BAND_TILT

Band slope (dy/dx) across the viewport.

BAND_WIDTH

Band thickness as a fraction of viewport height.

DIM_ALPHA

Alpha ceiling for the dimmest quartile of field stars.

SF_SCENE

Skybox sphere + starfield scales.

SKYBOX_RADIUS

Skybox sphere radius — wraps the whole multi-tier chart (the observable-universe shell clamps at ~46k units, the skybox must sit beyond it or the panorama would clip through the boundary).

SPHERE_SEGMENTS

Sphere tessellation — 256×128 ≈ 65k triangles per body, the ultra tier: at this density a planet's limb holds a smooth arc even at full-screen zoom and the terminator never facets under refraction in the fresnel shells. Catalog bodies stay resident (~150 meshes ≈ 9.8M tris, still trivially GPU-bound territory) while registry bodies ride the LRU spawn/evict path, so the budget holds.

ROCK_DETAIL

Icosahedron subdivision detail for irregular bodies (Phobos-class rubble moons, comet nuclei, catalog asteroids). detail is EDGE segments, not recursion depth — faces = 20·(d+1)², so detail 64 produces ~84.5k triangles (~42.5k welded verts): the crumpled silhouette stays continuous under glancing light at any zoom, no facet flash at the terminator and no visible polygon edges from afar. Only def.irregular bodies pay the density — a dozen catalog bodies at most.

ROCK_MID_FREQ

Mid/micro relief octaves for irregular bodies — a single low- frequency noise pass makes every body a smooth blob, so vnoise stacks three octaves: the macro crumple (1×) sets the silhouette, ROCK_MID_FREQ × adds the lumpy potato bumps real asteroids and rubble moons carry, and ROCK_FINE_FREQ × grains the surface at regolith scale (amplitudes are fractions of irregular.amp).

AMBIENT_INT

Fill-light intensity — kept low so the sun point light owns the terminator and planets shade with real day/night contrast instead of reading flat (a high ambient lifts the unlit hemisphere to nearly the lit-side brightness and washes out every texture).

SUN_INT

Sun point-light intensity at the scene origin (no decay).
